newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: ICO and UAE's Etisalat sign $33 mln satellite deal.
newsitem.headline: ICO and UAE's Etisalat sign $33 mln satellite deal.

text.p: ICO Global Communications said on Sunday it had signed a multi-year agreement worth $33 million with the Emirates Telecommunications Corporation (Etisalat) to operate one of its 12 global satellite access nodes (SANs).

"Etisalat will provide site infrastructure and operate the SANs which will be built in Dubai. Construction will begin in July, 1997," ICO, a London-based global satellite communications company, said in a statement.

A consortium led by NEC and including Ericsson and Hughes Network Systems will design, manufacture, construct and integrate all 12 SANs. Hughes Network Systems is a unit of Hughes Electronics Corp., which in turn is a subsidiary of General Motors Corp.

ICO was set up by 47 investors worldwide in 1995 to develop the International Mobile Satellite Organisation's (Inmarsat) satellite-based mobile telephone system. Inmarsat is a multinational cooperative based in London.
ICO, with current capitalisation of $1.5 billion, will begin full operation in 2000.
Etisalat, which is owned 60 percent by the United Arab Emirates government and 40 percent by private investors, has a 4.5 percent stake in ICO.
